provenance: This is an enterprise content management system's document library and upload console — the family of SharePoint document libraries, Box, Egnyte, M-Files, Alfresco and OpenText Content Server — together with the integration developer portal such platforms ship. What led there: each record is one stored document carrying an opaque document identifier, a file name, a byte size that may be unreported, an internet media type, a display label distinct from the file name, an ingestion state drawn from a ready/uploading/failed set, and a flag saying whether it is staged for the next upload. That is a document-library row plus a transfer, not a business entity. The policy object reinforces it: an allowlist of accepted media types, a maximum file-name length, a rows-per-page size, a size-unit base of 1024, a set of transfer states, a keyboard key that submits an upload, and a set of preview viewport widths — this is exactly the administration surface of a document library, not application domain configuration. The contract then describes list rows carrying accessible labels, a size string with a fallback for unreported sizes, a priority-ordered upload hint, a per-row checkbox that toggles selection, and an upload dialog submitted by form or by keyboard — i.e. the published behaviour contract for a document library's list view and batch-upload modal.
reference_products: Microsoft SharePoint Online document libraries (the market leader; also OneDrive for Business, which shares the same list surface) - contributed the whole library screen: a white canvas with a narrow left site rail (Home / Documents / Shared with us / Site contents / Recycle bin / Edit), a ghost-button command bar above the list (+ New, Upload, Sync, Export to Excel, Automate, ...) with the view controls pushed to the far right (All Items v, filter funnel, info (i), expand arrows), and a column-header row whose headers are themselves the sort/filter menus (Ascending / Descending / Clear filters from Modified, with A-Z / Z-A glyphs). Also supplied the exact column vocabulary the domain has settled on - DocIcon, Name, Modified, Modified By, File Size, Checked Out To, Created, Created By, ID - and the two surfaces that hang off the toolbar: the 'Edit view columns' right panel (pale-blue command strip with a save glyph + 'Apply' and an x, heading, small grey helper paragraph, a plain checkbox list where checked entries are bold) and the 'Add column' popover (Single line of text / Number / Person / Date / More... / hairline / Show or hide columns). The density menu 'List / Compact list' is where the rows-per-page and row-height vocabulary lives.

Box - web app plus Box UI Elements (Content Explorer, Content Uploader) and the Box developer portal. Contributed the integration-developer half of this environment: a thin top tab strip (Home / AI / API reference / Tools / Tutorials / Changelog), a left nav tree that nests three levels deep with chevrons and a rounded pale-blue full-width pill on the active leaf, endpoint entries prefixed by small saturated method chips (GET green, POST blue, PUT amber, DEL red), a centred prose column at roughly a 640px measure, and a sticky right rail that is either an 'On this page' anchor list or the request/response pair. Its reference page is the model for the console: an endpoint line rendered as `GET / files / {file_id}` with the path parameter in a green-tinted mono chip and a filled 'Try it >' button beside it; a cURL sample card with a language selector and copy affordance; and a response card tabbed by status code (200 | 401 | 404 | 405 | 415 | default) with a plain-text tab row and a 2px underline on the active tab. Parameter rows read as blue mono name, small grey type chip, small grey location chip, then a red-tinted 'required' pill. Also the source of the version banner ('This endpoint is in the version 2024.0...') as a pale-blue info card with an (i) glyph - the shape the developer center's revision/encoding preamble should take.

Egnyte - Web UI plus the Egnyte for Developers portal. Contributed the flatter, calmer variant of the same developer chrome: a single alphabetical 'DOCS NAVIGATION' list (no nesting) where the active entry gets a 3px coloured left bar and a coloured label instead of a filled pill, H2 sections each closed by a full-width hairline, near-black code blocks for base URLs and headers, inline code as a pale tinted chip with magenta text and no border, and 'Note:' callouts as pale-green cards with a green left rule. Its section vocabulary is close to what this contract needs verbatim - Base URL, Authentication, Important Notes, Upload a File, List File or Folder, Chunked Upload, Error Codes, Related Resources. On the product side Egnyte's Web UI is the reference for sorting by clicking the column name (item name, size, date modified) and for the Upload Request / 'Ways to upload files' framing of a staged batch. Supporting look at OpenText Documentum Content Management for the workspace-landing vocabulary its product mock uses: File Library, My Collections, Document List, Recycle Bin, Add file, Upload file, Upload folder, Workflow overview, 'Item cannot be accessed.'

design_tokens.palette: Light only, and far emptier than a generated ECM screen usually is. Page chrome sits on a very light warm neutral (#FAF9F8 / #F5F5F5); the library canvas, cards, panels and dialogs are pure white (#FFFFFF) on top of it. Text is a near-black #242424 for primary content (file names, values, headings), #616161 for every secondary string (column headers, metadata columns, helper text, breadcrumb ancestors, key labels in the properties surface), #A19F9D for placeholders and disabled. Exactly one blue does all interactive work: #0F6CBD (Box's #0061D5 is the same role) for links, the primary filled button, the checked-checkbox fill, the active nav item's label and its 2-3px left bar, and the active tab underline. Nothing decorative is blue. Selection and hover are tints of that blue at the very bottom of its range - hover row #F5F5F5, selected row #EBF3FC - never a border, never a left accent on the row. Hairlines are #E1DFDD / #EDEBE9 at 1px; tables carry a hairline under the header row and between rows and NO vertical rules at all, and no zebra striping ever. Status colour exists only inside small chips and 12-16px glyphs, never as a row background or a card border: green #107C10 for ready/complete, amber #C19C00 (fill #EAA300 for a progress bar) for in-flight transfers, red #C50F1F for failed and for the 'required' pill in the reference. A chip is the hue at ~10% as background with the full-strength hue as text. The developer center is the only place saturated pills appear at all (the GET/POST/PUT/DEL method chips) and the only place a dark surface appears (near-black #1B1F23 code blocks with mono text; inline code instead gets a #F0F0F0 chip, 2px radius, no border). What is deliberately absent: no gradients anywhere, no coloured page headers or coloured sidebars, no coloured table headers, no tinted card borders, no full-width alert banners for ordinary states, no illustrations in empty states, and no shadow on anything that is not a popover or a dialog.
design_tokens.typography: One neutral humanist sans for all UI - 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', -apple-system, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial - and one mono for machine strings: ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', Consolas, 'SF Mono', monospace. Scale: 13-14px/20px for table cells, form values and body prose; 12px/16px for column headers, metadata, breadcrumbs, helper paragraphs and chip text; 16px/22px semibold for section headings and dialog titles; 20-24px semibold for the page title; 28-32px for the developer-center article H1 (documentation pages run one step larger than the app, exactly as Box's and SharePoint's do). Only two weights - 400 and 600. Column headers are 12px 600 in #616161, not uppercase and not letter-spaced. No italics except a single 'Applies to' style aside. Byte sizes, counts and page ranges use tabular lining figures so the size column stays aligned; the size string is never right-aligned into its own gutter - it sits left-aligned in its column like every other cell, which is what the real libraries do. Mono at 12.5-13px carries every opaque machine value: the document identifier, the internet media type (application/pdf), event names, JSON keys and payloads, the keyboard key ('Enter'), and endpoint paths. Keyboard keys in the shortcuts overlay render as a kbd chip: 11px mono, #FFFFFF fill, 1px #D1D1D1 border, 3px radius, 1px bottom shadow.
design_tokens.density: Comfortable-but-tight, on a 4px grid. Table rows 44px tall (the 'compact list' variant is 36px); the header row is the same height as a body row with no fill of its own. The leading checkbox column is a fixed 44px, checkbox 16px square with a 3px radius, and the header checkbox shows the indeterminate dash when the page is partly selected. Cells get 8px vertical / 12px horizontal padding; the name cell leads with a 16-20px file-type glyph, an 8px gap, then the name - and the name is the only clickable text in the row. Command bar 40-44px tall, its buttons ghost (transparent until hover, then #F5F5F5), 4px radius, icon at 16px + label at 13px with an 8px gap, groups separated by a 1px vertical hairline and 8px of air. Page title block sits 24px above the command bar; 16px between the command bar and the header row. Right details panel 320-360px wide, 20px padding, key/value pairs stacked (12px #616161 label above a 14px #242424 value) with 16px between pairs and a hairline between groups - never a two-column table. Dialogs 480-560px wide, 24px padding, title 16px 600, footer buttons right-aligned with 8px between them. Popovers anchored to their trigger, 200-280px wide, 4px padding, 32px item rows. Paging footer is a single 40px row under the table, left-aligned range text with the pager on the right.
design_tokens.components: Left rail 220-260px, same white as the canvas (not a tinted panel), items 32-36px tall at 13px, active item gets a #F0F0F0 pill plus a 3px #0F6CBD left bar and a 600 label; groups separated by 16px of space rather than a rule; the recycle-bin style utility entry sits at the bottom, detached. Breadcrumb above the page title at 12-13px: ancestors in #616161 that turn #0F6CBD on hover, '>' or '/' separators in #A19F9D, current segment plain #242424 and not a link. Buttons: primary is filled #0F6CBD with white 13px 600 text, 4px radius, 8px/16px padding; secondary is white with a 1px #8A8886 border and #242424 text; toolbar buttons are ghost. Inputs 32px tall, 1px #8A8886 border, 4px radius, and on focus a 2px #0F6CBD bottom rule rather than a full glowing ring. Status chips are 20-22px pills at 11-12px with 8px horizontal padding and a 10-11px leading dot or glyph. A transfer in flight renders as a 4px-tall #EAA300 track inside its row's status cell plus the state word beside it - not a large progress card. Tabs (settings sections, response status codes) are plain 13px text on the canvas with 12px horizontal padding and a 2px #0F6CBD underline on the active one; there is no tab container, no pill background, no border box. Modal for a batch upload: title, a dashed 1px #C8C6C4 drop area with a centred one-line prompt and a 'Browse' link, then a dense table of staged items (name / size / state) at the same 44px rhythm, then a right-aligned footer with a filled primary and a plain-white cancel; the submit affordance names its keyboard equivalent in the helper text rather than in a tooltip. Developer center: three columns - nav tree, a 640-740px prose measure, sticky right rail - with H2s closed by a full-width hairline, code blocks near-black with 12.5px mono and a copy affordance at the top-right, note callouts as pale-tinted cards with a 3px coloured left rule, and parameter tables rendered as stacked rows (blue mono name, grey type chip, grey location chip, red 'required' pill, then a 13px description paragraph) rather than as a real grid. Empty state is one line of #616161 13px text plus at most one link, centred in the list body - no illustration, no card.
design_tokens.spacing: 4px base unit; the usable steps are 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48. Page gutter 24px at desktop, 32px on very wide screens; the list itself is allowed to run the full content width while prose is capped at ~740px and the whole content column at ~1280px. Vertical rhythm: 24px between a page title and the first control, 16px between a control strip and the content it governs, 32px between major sections on a settings or documentation page, 12px inside a card between a label and its value. Radii: 4px on buttons, inputs, cards, dialogs and popovers; 3px on checkboxes and inline code; 12px (fully rounded) only on status chips and method chips. Elevation is almost entirely absent - the only shadowed surfaces are popovers, dropdowns and dialogs, at 0 8px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.14) over an 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.12) ambient; panels, cards, toolbars and tables get a hairline instead of a shadow, and never both. Responsive: at the 600px breakpoint the table drops its secondary columns to a stacked two-line row (name over a metadata line), the left rail collapses to a hamburger, the details panel becomes a full-width sheet, and the modal goes edge-to-edge with 16px gutters; long file names and media types wrap with overflow-wrap rather than truncating with an ellipsis, so nothing ever forces a horizontal scrollbar at 375 / 768 / 1024.

structural_notes:
These products all put navigation in a persistent left rail that lists places, not actions: the workspace home, the shared document library, a system-managed governance/records collection, library administration, and the developer center, with the recycle bin detached at the bottom. A slim top bar carries the workspace switcher at far left, a centred search field with a keyboard-shortcut hint in it, and the account avatar plus a shortcuts/help entry at right. Under it sits a breadcrumb, then the page title, then a command bar - and the command bar is where every overlay in this environment is launched from (Upload, the transfer monitor, the responsive-preview presets, the view/column controls), which is why none of those surfaces needs its own nav entry.

The list-to-detail relationship is the single most distinctive thing to copy: the list never navigates away. Clicking a document's name opens the built-in previewer; clicking the info glyph, or a row's overflow menu, opens the properties surface as a right-hand panel (or, in newer SharePoint, a centred dialog) while the list stays rendered and the row stays highlighted behind it. Properties are a stacked key/value read-out - identifier, file name, display label, media type, size, transfer state - not a table and not an editable form by default. Selection is a separate axis from opening: the per-row checkbox only stages the item, the header checkbox stages the page, and the count of staged items is echoed in the command bar and carried into the upload dialog. Sorting lives in the column header itself, not in a separate sort control, and the header menu mixes sort directions with filter entries and a 'clear filters from this column' item. Rows-per-page is a library setting, exposed in administration, and reflected in the list only as a 'x-y of n' range plus a pager in a footer strip.

Chrome around the content is made of hairlines and whitespace, essentially nothing else: no card wraps the table, no border boxes the tabs, no panel background distinguishes the sidebar from the canvas. Administration is a full page with a horizontal tab row (General / Content types), each setting a labelled row with the value or control right-aligned - accepted media types and transfer states appear there as lists of chips, and appear nowhere else in the product. The developer center is its own three-column area with a version-and-encoding preamble at the top of its landing page and a runnable request builder hanging off the endpoint reference, whose response body is shown in a status-tabbed card.

Vocabulary to use throughout: Documents, Library, Items, Name, Display name, Modified, Modified by, Location, File size, Type, Content type, Transfer state, Staged for upload, Checked out to, Version history, Properties, Details pane, Show or hide columns, Switch view options, List / Compact list, Recycle bin, Site contents, Upload, Upload folder, Sync, Add column. Units and formats: sizes render as '0 B', '1.5 KB', '2 MB' on a 1024 base with one decimal place and the unit separated by a space, and an unreported size reads as the literal fallback string rather than a dash or a zero; counts read as '4 items'; paging reads as '1-3 of 4'; the media type is shown as the raw internet media type string (application/pdf, text/markdown) on the properties surface and in the developer center, but as a friendly type name in the list's type column; viewport presets are labelled in raw pixels (375 / 768 / 1024) with a device word beside them; keyboard bindings render as kbd chips ('Enter'). Every row exposes an accessible name built from the file name and the size string, and the checkbox, not the row, is the keyboard-selectable control.
